aum.raw: NT$77.232 billion total cost across 70 direct-investment companies (as of Dec 2024)

strategy.thesis: Taiwan's flagship government investment fund. Accelerates industrial innovation and economic transformation via direct industrial investment, indirect investment as an LP in venture-capital funds, business-angel co-investment and loan financing; acts as a co-investor (not lead, capped at 20% of equity) alongside private capital.

track_record.portfolio_count: 70 direct-investment companies (Dec 2024); 35 active investments per CB Insights

application.how_to_apply: Apply to a specific NDF program (direct investment, Industry Innovation & Transformation Fund, Business Angel Investment Program, VC fund investment) via the NDF Management Committee or its project offices

summary.en: The National Development Fund (國發基金) is Taiwan's flagship government investment fund, operating under the Executive Yuan's NDF Management Committee. Established in its current form on 1 Oct 2006 (by merging the Executive Yuan Development Fund, founded 1973, with the Sino-American Fund), it accelerates industrial innovation through direct industrial investment, acting as an LP in venture-capital funds, business-angel co-investment and loan financing. As of Dec 2024 it had invested in 70 direct-investment companies at a total cost of NT$77.232 billion, always as a co-investor (capped at 20% of equity, never the lead).
summary.local: 行政院國家發展基金(國發基金)為臺灣最重要的政府投資基金,由行政院國家發展基金管理會管理。現制於 2006 年 10 月 1 日由行政院開發基金(1973 年成立)與中美經濟社會發展基金合併設立。透過直接產業投資、作為創投基金的有限合夥人(LP)、創業天使共同投資及貸款融資加速產業創新。截至 2024 年 12 月,已直接投資 70 家事業,投資總成本達新臺幣 772.32 億元,且一律為共同投資人(持股上限 20%,不擔任主投資人)。

strategy.thesis: Government co-investment scheme run by the National Development Fund alongside qualified angel investors, accelerators and VC firms, providing early-stage capital plus mentoring and networking to innovative Taiwanese startups; the NDF matches private angel capital rather than leading rounds.

summary.en: The NDF Business Angel Investment Program (創業天使投資方案) is a National Development Fund co-investment scheme launched in late 2018. The NDF invests alongside qualified angels, accelerators and VC firms in early Taiwanese startups (established <8 years, paid-in capital ≤NT$100M), investing up to NT$20M per case (first investment up to NT$30M, cumulative up to NT$100M). Originally budgeted at NT$1bn, it was scaled up to NT$10bn and runs until end-2030. As of 31 Aug 2022 it had backed 202 startups with NT$3.162bn of approved angel investment, crowding in NT$8.818bn of private capital.
summary.local: 行政院國家發展基金創業天使投資方案於 2018 年底推出,由國發基金與合格天使投資人、加速器及創投共同投資台灣早期新創(設立未逾 8 年、實收資本額或累計募資不超過新臺幣 1 億元),對同一事業投資以不超過 2,000 萬元為原則(初次最高 3,000 萬元、累計最高 1 億元)。初始預算 10 億元,後擴大為 100 億元,受理至民國 119 年(2030 年)底。截至 2022 年 8 月 31 日已投資 202 家新創,核定天使投資 31.62 億元,帶動民間投資 88.18 億元。

strategy.thesis: Government-initiated venture-capital firm sponsored by the National Development Fund (40% owner) to channel private capital into Taiwan's strategic sectors — IoT/semiconductors, biotech and deep tech — and connect Taiwanese technology with international markets including the US and Central & Eastern Europe.

summary.en: Taiwania Capital (台杉投資) is a government-initiated venture-capital firm founded in August 2017, sponsored by the National Development Fund (40% ownership) to mobilise private capital into Taiwan's strategic sectors. It focuses on IoT/semiconductors, biotech and deep tech and connects Taiwanese tech to the US and, since 2022, Central & Eastern Europe (a US$200M fund). By Aug 2021 it had raised about US$490M (NT$13.75bn) across five funds; AUM reached about US$1bn by 2024, with 75+ companies invested and IPO exits including Ambiq Micro, C4 Therapeutics and Fractyl Health.

summary.en: SBIR (小型企業創新研發計畫) is a non-dilutive R&D grant program run by Taiwan's SME and Startup Administration (MOEA). It subsidises innovation by domestic SMEs across three phases: Phase 1 (prior research) up to NT$1.5M over 6 months; Phase 2 (R&D) up to NT$6M per year and NT$12M total over 2 years; and Phase 2+ (value-added application) up to NT$6M over up to 1 year. Eligible applicants are domestic SMEs with paid-in capital under NT$100M or fewer than 200 employees; applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

strategy.thesis: MOEA (Industrial Development Administration / former Department of Industrial Technology) matching R&D grant guiding enterprises to invest in forward-looking, cross-domain industrial technology development; subsidises forefront technology R&D, integrated R&D and the establishment of in-Taiwan R&D centres.

summary.en: The A+ Industrial Innovative R&D Program (A+企業創新研發淬鍊計畫) is a MOEA matching R&D grant launched in 2014 (then under the Department of Industrial Technology, now the Industrial Development Administration). It guides enterprises to invest in forward-looking, cross-domain industrial technology through three tracks — forefront technology R&D, integrated R&D, and establishing R&D centres in Taiwan. The subsidy covers in principle 40% and up to a maximum 50% of total project cost, with the remainder self-funded. Eligible applicants are domestic, legally-registered, financially-sound, non-Chinese-invested businesses.

aka: Startup Island Taiwan national startup brand

strategy.thesis: National startup brand and promotion program led by the National Development Council to raise the global visibility of Taiwanese startups. Its 'NEXT BIG' initiative selects benchmark startups (recommended by the community and industry leaders) and supports them with branding, overseas business-development and international investment connections.

application_cycles: NEXT BIG annual selection / community recommendation
program.eligibility: Taiwanese startups (the brand badge is free to use by all the country's startups; NEXT BIG is curated/recommended)

summary.en: Startup Island TAIWAN is the national startup brand jointly created by the National Development Council (NDC) and Taiwan's startup communities, launched and branded around 2020–2021 to raise the global visibility of Taiwanese startups (the badge/logo is free for any local startup to use). Its flagship 'NEXT BIG' program, launched in 2021 with nine startups (a further 13 added in 2023, 22 total), identifies benchmark startups — such as AmazingTalker and Hahow — and supports them with branding, overseas business development and international investment connections rather than direct funding.
summary.local: Startup Island TAIWAN 為國家發展委員會(NDC)與台灣新創社群共同打造的國家新創品牌,約於 2020–2021 年推出並建立品牌識別,提升台灣新創的國際能見度(品牌標誌開放全國新創免費使用)。旗艦的「NEXT BIG」計畫於 2021 年推出、首選 9 家新創(2023 年再增 13 家,共 22 家),選拔指標性新創(如 AmazingTalker、Hahow),以品牌、海外商機與國際投資連結等方式支持,而非直接出資。

verification_notes: Startup Island TAIWAN is primarily a national branding/promotion program (no direct cash or equity), included here as a government public program. The brand was launched around 2020–2021 (NDC branding event reported Dec; founded_year set to 2020 as approximate); NEXT BIG cohorts are 2021 (9) and 2023 (13).
